title: ～ても構わない — “I don't mind if ～ / it's all right to ～”
summary: Verb te-form + も + 構わない gives permission or says a condition does not matter: “it's fine to ～ / I don't mind if ～.” It is a polite way to allow something, and also to say that a worse situation is acceptable.

patterns.form: 動詞て形／い形容詞くて／名詞・な形容詞で ＋ も ＋ 構わない
patterns.gloss: te-form / い-adj くて / noun, な-adj で + も + 構わない
Polite: 〜ても構いません (座っても構いません)

body.p: 構う means “to mind, to care.” 構わない is “it doesn't matter.” With ても, the whole phrase means “even if ～, it doesn't matter.” 座っても構いません sounds like “you may sit, I don't mind.”
It is a softer, more polite alternative to ～てもいいです. It often appears in notices and in replies to a request: ここで写真を撮っても構いません (photos are allowed here).
The speaker can also say that a less ideal situation is acceptable: 少し遅れても構いませんので、必ず来てください. Be careful: with a negative (～なくても構わない), it means “it is not necessary to ～.”

examples.ja: ここに座（すわ）っても構（かま）いません。
examples.tr: I don't mind if you sit here.

examples.ja: 少（すこ）し遅（おく）れても構（かま）いませんので、必（かなら）ず来（き）てください。
examples.romaji: Sukoshi okurete mo kamaimasen node, kanarazu kite kudasai.
examples.tr: I don't mind if you're a little late, so please be sure to come.

examples.ja: 写真（しゃしん）はこの部屋（へや）で撮（と）っても構（かま）いません。
examples.romaji: Shashin wa kono heya de totte mo kamaimasen.
examples.tr: It's fine to take photos in this room.

pitfalls: In a question, ～ても構いませんか asks for permission politely. Answer with はい、構いません or どうぞ.
Do not confuse ～てもかまわない (permission) with ～なくてもかまわない (not necessary).
